bugs.creator: kevinushey
bugs.summary: scan() reads past its field buffer when stripping a UTF-8 BOM from a buffer-filling first field

comments.creator: kevinushey
comments.text:
When scan() strips a UTF-8 byte-order mark from the first field, it reads up to 3 bytes past the end of its field buffer. The over-read is read-only, but it is undefined behaviour and has been present since BOM support was added in R 3.0.0.

Reproducible example (UTF-8 locale, visible under AddressSanitizer):

    x <- paste0("﻿", strrep("a", 8186))   # 8189 bytes with the BOM
    scan(text = x, what = "", quiet = TRUE)

    ==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow
    READ of size 8190 at 0x6250022df100
        #0 __asan_memmove
        #1 fillBuffer scan.c:468
        #2 scanVector scan.c:610
    0x6250022df100 is located 0 bytes after 8192-byte region
        allocated by R_AllocStringBuffer memory.c:4970

Expected: strrep("a", 8186) with no sanitizer report. A file connection behaves the same way.

Analysis:

fillBuffer() in src/main/scan.c strips the BOM with

    memmove(buffer->data, buffer->data+3, strlen(buffer->data) + 1);

copying from offset 3 but with the length of the whole string, so every strip reads 3 bytes past the terminator. The buffer grows only when the write index reaches nbuf - 3, so a first field of exactly nbuf - 3 bytes (8189 for the initial buffer) leaves the NUL in the last slot and the over-read leaves the allocation. The other BOM-stripping sites (connections.c, sysutils.c) use offsets or explicit lengths and are fine.

Proposed patch: attached as scan-bom-overread.diff (against r90668). It uses strlen(buffer->data+3) + 1 and adds a regression test to tests/reg-tests-1e.R. Verified with an ASan build and make check on macOS.

Found by OSS-Fuzz (libFuzzer_r_scan, testcase 5435960603770880).

The patch is also submitted as https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/377, where CI results can be seen.
